methodology:
Methodology

This document records every assumption, transformation, aggregation rule and statistical choice. Numeric results are deliberately not written here — they are produced by the code (reports/findings.md, the dashboard) so they always match the data.

1. Guiding principles

  1. Model output is not measurement. All PM2.5 in this project is modelled. Statements describe the model output, and are labelled as such in every view.
  2. Sources stay separate. World Bank (daily) and Kaggle/HF (hourly) PM2.5 come from different models, at different resolutions, for different periods. They are never averaged together; they are compared only on matched city-days.
  3. Concentrations are not converted to AQI. The WHO 2021 guideline values (24-hour 15 µg/m³, annual 5 µg/m³) appear only as reference lines/thresholds.
  4. Flag, don't delete. Values that are physically impossible are excluded and logged; values that are merely unusual are flagged and kept, with optional exclusion in the dashboard.
  5. Independent units for inference. Daily values within a city are serially dependent and are never treated as independent samples in a test.

2. Pipeline (scripts/prepare_data.py → src/data/pipeline.py)

The pipeline rebuilds every processed table from data/raw on each run and overwrites outputs atomically (write to .tmp, then rename). Repeated runs therefore cannot accumulate duplicates; a test re-runs it and compares row counts.

2.1 Loading and normalisation

  • CSV and Parquet are supported (src/data/load.py). Raw files are only read.
  • Column names: NFKC-normalised, lower-cased, punctuation → _, then mapped through a synonym table (pm2_5/PM2.5 → pm25, relative_humidity_2m_mean → humidity, …). Collisions raise an error.
  • City names: NFKC, whitespace collapsed, title-cased, alias table (e.g. "Islamabad Capital Territory" → "Islamabad"). A separate matching key strips everything except letters/digits (so "Arif Wala" and "Arifwala" collide and are flagged).
  • Dates: parsed with errors="coerce"; unparseable values are excluded and logged. Time-zone-aware input is converted to the target zone and made naive; naive input is localised only when a source zone is known.

2.2 Validation and exclusions (src/data/validate.py, src/data/clean.py)

Check World Bank (single-value rows) Kaggle/HF & ERA5 (multi-variable rows)
Unparseable date row excluded row excluded
Non-numeric value row excluded cell → NaN
Missing value row excluded kept as NaN
Outside plausible range (PLAUSIBLE_RANGES in src/utils/config.py) row excluded cell → NaN
Exact duplicate key + values duplicates dropped (one kept) same
Conflicting duplicate key (values differ) all copies excluded (no arbitrary choice) same
Country ≠ PAK excluded –
PM2.5 > PM10 – flagged

Each action is written to data/processed/exclusions_log.csv.

2.3 Place identity

  • Province labels. The source provides only ADM1 codes. Labels were assigned from the undisputed capital found inside each code (PAK002 Quetta → Balochistan, PAK003 Islamabad → ICT, PAK005 Peshawar → Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, PAK006 Lahore → Punjab, PAK007 Hyderabad → Sindh). The pipeline re-verifies these anchors on every run (adm1_anchor_check in the manifest). No boundary file is used, so a place's province is only as good as its source code; a nearest-neighbour consistency check lists candidates for review.
  • Disambiguated labels. Places sharing a name get "(Province)" or, if still ambiguous, coordinates.
  • Identical series. Places whose complete daily series are identical (SHA-1 of the rounded series) are grouped. Descriptive views keep all places; inferential tests keep one representative (most populous) per group.
  • Coordinates are never corrected, even when they look wrong (e.g. a name/coordinate mismatch); they are flagged instead.

2.4 Model-artifact screen (src/analysis/data_quality.py)

Two diagnostics, both computed per place on the World Bank series: 1. Fixed annual mean — longest run of consecutive complete calendar years whose annual means differ by < 0.5 % from the previous year. Real annual concentrations normally vary by several percent; a run of ≥ 3 such years suggests the model scales daily values to a fixed annual level. 2. Abrupt level shift — for every candidate break (≥ 12 months each side) in the deseasonalised monthly anomaly series, a Welch t-statistic for the change in mean; the maximum is kept. Flag when t ≥ 10 and the shift is ≥ 30 % of the place's mean level. Because the maximum over many breaks inflates t, this is a screening rule, not a formal change-point test.

Flagged places are kept by default. The dashboard offers a global toggle to exclude them, and reports show key results with and without them.

2.5 Outliers

Robust z-score on log PM2.5 within each place: z = 0.6745 · (log x − median) / MAD; flag when |z| > 3.5 (Iglewicz & Hoaglin). Logs are used because concentrations are right-skewed. Box plots separately use Tukey fences (1.5 × IQR) for display only.

3. Temporal rules

Aggregation Rule
hourly → daily (Kaggle/HF) mean (precipitation sum, wind direction circular mean); requires ≥ 18 valid hours
daily → monthly mean of daily values; month complete with ≥ 20 valid days
monthly → annual mean of complete monthly means (so months are equally weighted); year complete with ≥ 11 complete months
rolling means centred, calendar-aware (gaps are not bridged); require ≥ 70 % of the window

The World Bank series lacks the last day of every month (detected by the gap analysis), so complete months have one day fewer than calendar months; the 20-day rule is unaffected.

Time zones. World Bank days have an undocumented boundary. ERA5 weather was requested for the local day (Asia/Karachi). Weather–PM2.5 lagged correlations at ±1 day are reported to show sensitivity to this mismatch. Kaggle/HF timestamps are kept exactly as labelled; a diagnostic compares the hour of peak ozone with the hour of peak temperature (both normally peak in the early-to-mid afternoon) and reports the offset.

Seasons (project definition aligned with the monsoon cycle): Winter Dec–Feb, Spring Mar–Apr, Pre-monsoon May–Jun, Monsoon Jul–Sep, Post-monsoon Oct–Nov.

Weekend = Saturday and Sunday. Official weekends in Pakistan have changed over time, and daily models may not resolve weekly emission cycles; weekday results are therefore descriptive.

4. Statistical methods

Every test returns: question, null hypothesis, unit of analysis, n, assumptions (and checks), statistic, p-value, effect size (with bootstrap CI where meaningful) and an interpretation generated from the numbers.

Question Unit Method Effect size
Do seasons differ? city (seasonal median) Friedman test, cities as blocks; pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank with Holm correction Kendall's W; matched-pairs rank-biserial
Do provinces differ? city (overall median) Kruskal–Wallis (groups with < 3 cities excluded); pairwise Mann–Whitney with Holm ε²; rank-biserial
Same, parametric city (mean) One-way ANOVA only if Shapiro–Wilk (each group) and Levene do not reject at α = 0.05; otherwise reported as "not justified" η²
Weekday vs weekend city (difference of means) Wilcoxon signed-rank median difference (µg/m³ and % of level), bootstrap CI, rank-biserial
Change between two complete years city (annual means) Wilcoxon signed-rank median % change, bootstrap CI; counts up/down
Weather association city (one Spearman ρ per city) per-city ρ with autocorrelation-adjusted p (effective n, Bretherton et al. 1999), BH-FDR across cities; one-sample Wilcoxon on the ρ values median ρ with bootstrap CI
Long-term trend per city monthly anomalies OLS with Newey–West (HAC, 12 lags) CI; Theil–Sen slope; BH-FDR across cities slope µg/m³/yr and % of level per year

Deseasonalisation. For trends and anomaly correlations, each value is reduced by the place's mean for that calendar month. Pollution and weather share a strong annual cycle, so raw correlations largely reflect seasonality; anomaly correlations describe day-to-day co-variation.

Effective sample size. n_eff = n (1 − r₁ₓr₁ᵧ)/(1 + r₁ₓr₁ᵧ) with lag-1 autocorrelations r₁. p-values and confidence intervals for correlations are recomputed with n_eff.

Multiple comparisons. Holm within each family of pairwise contrasts; Benjamini–Hochberg FDR across cities; Holm across the family of headline tests on the Statistical Analysis page.

Significance vs importance. With hundreds of cities and years of data, tiny effects reach p < 0.05. Effect sizes, confidence intervals and differences in µg/m³ are always shown, and interpretation text calls out statistically significant but practically negligible effects.

Remaining dependence. Cities are treated as independent units, but neighbouring cities share regional meteorology and the modelled surface is spatially smooth, so city-level p-values remain somewhat optimistic. This caveat is attached to every test result.

5. Sensitivity analysis (src/analysis/sensitivity.py)

The same headline metrics (overall median, median of city medians, top city, overlap of the top-10, Spearman correlation of city rankings with the baseline) are recomputed under: baseline · outliers excluded · winsorised at 1st/99th percentiles · complete calendar years only · last three complete years · winter excluded · one place per identical series · artifact-flagged places excluded.

6. Source comparison

Each Kaggle/HF city is paired with the nearest World Bank place within 25 km (haversine). On shared dates the report gives n, medians, mean bias, MAE, ratio of medians and Pearson r with an autocorrelation-adjusted CI. Agreement or disagreement indicates model uncertainty; neither source is treated as truth.

7. Known limitations

  • No ground-truth monitor data; all conclusions concern model estimates.
  • The World Bank model shows fixed annual levels and abrupt shifts for many places (see the artifact screen); rankings and trends for those places reflect model behaviour.
  • Units of the World Bank PM2.5 field are not stated by the source (assumed µg/m³).
  • Kaggle/HF data have unknown licence and provenance, cover only one winter, and show a likely timestamp misalignment between pollutant and weather columns.
  • ERA5 is 0.25° reanalysis; it does not resolve urban microclimates. Weather was fetched for 22 places only.
  • Province labels come from source codes, not a boundary overlay.
  • Population figures are GeoNames values of unknown vintage.
data_sources:
Data sources

Three sources were acquired and verified on 2026-10-24. None contains monitor measurements: all are model or reanalysis products, and each is labelled value_type = "modelled" in the processed tables. Sources are cleaned and analysed separately; they are never pooled row-wise.

ID Source Values Resolution Licence Used for
wb_pm25 World Bank — Daily City-Level PM2.5 Estimates 2018–2026 (Global PM2.5 Watch) PM2.5, modelled daily, per place CC BY-SA 4.0 primary analytical dataset
hf_aq Pakistan Air Quality & Weather (10 Cities) — Kaggle dataset mirrored on Hugging Face PM2.5, PM10, CO, NO₂, SO₂, O₃, dust + weather; modelled (probable CAMS) hourly unknown hourly/diurnal views, source comparison
openmeteo_era5 Open-Meteo Historical Weather API, ERA5 model temperature, humidity, dew point, wind, precipitation, pressure daily (local day) CC BY 4.0 weather relationships

1. World Bank Global PM2.5 Watch (wb_pm25)

  • Catalogue page: https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0067162/daily-city-level-air-pollution-pm2-5-estimates-2018-2026
  • File used: PM25_Middle_East_North_Africa_Afghanistan_Pakistan.zip (≈ 75.5 MB zipped, one ≈ 1 GB CSV) https://datacatalogfiles.worldbank.org/ddh-published/0067162/DR0096340/PM25_Middle_East_North_Africa_Afghanistan_Pakistan.zip
  • Licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 (as stated on the catalogue page). Derived tables in data/processed/ inherit the share-alike condition.
  • Method (from the catalogue): machine-learning estimates combining IQAir monitor data, TROPOMI satellite retrievals, ERA5 reanalysis, EDGAR emissions, Köppen–Geiger climate zones, MERIT-DEM elevation and coastal indicators.
  • Schema as downloaded: wb_region, nam_0, adm0_wb_a3, pm25_iso3, adm1cd_c, geonameid, city, latitude, longitude, population, date, pm25.
  • Units: the catalogue page does not state units. Values are treated as µg/m³ because (a) PM2.5 concentrations are conventionally reported in µg/m³, (b) the value range is consistent with published PM2.5 levels for South Asia. This is an assumption and is stated wherever values are shown.
  • Pakistan extraction: rows with adm0_wb_a3 == "PAK" are streamed out of the regional CSV by scripts/extract_worldbank_pakistan.py into data/raw/worldbank_pm25/worldbank_pm25_pakistan_subset.parquet. The original zip is never modified. The South Asia regional file was not downloaded because the MENA file explicitly covers Pakistan; whether Pakistan also appears there was not verified.
  • Day boundary / time zone: not documented by the source.

2. Kaggle / Hugging Face hourly dataset (hf_aq)

  • Hugging Face mirror (downloaded): https://huggingface.co/datasets/jason1966/ahsanneural_pakistan-air-quality-and-weather-10-cities → pakistan_air_quality_final_clean.csv (3,778,678 bytes)
  • Original Kaggle page (named in the mirror's card): https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/ahsanneural/pakistan-air-quality-and-weather-10-cities — the page's metadata could not be read without a Kaggle login, so the original description and licence were not verified.
  • Licence: unknown in the Hugging Face card. Treat as not cleared for redistribution; it is used here for non-commercial analysis only. Remove it from any public deployment if that is a concern (the app runs without it — hourly views then show an explained empty state).
  • Provenance: undocumented. Column names (pm2_5, carbon_monoxide, nitrogen_dioxide, sulphur_dioxide, ozone, dust) match the Open-Meteo Air Quality API, whose global pollutant data come from the CAMS atmospheric model; values are therefore labelled modelled.
  • Known issues found during the audit: pollutant and weather columns appear to use different time references (≈ 6-hour offset in diurnal peaks); Islamabad and Rawalpindi share identical series for most variables; source-derived aqi_category and calendar columns are dropped and recomputed.

3. Open-Meteo ERA5 weather (openmeteo_era5)

  • API: https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive with models=era5, timezone=Asia/Karachi. Docs: https://open-meteo.com/en/docs/historical-weather-api
  • Licence: Open-Meteo API data are offered under CC BY 4.0 (https://open-meteo.com/en/licence); underlying ERA5 data from the Copernicus Climate Change Service.
  • Model: ERA5 reanalysis, 0.25° grid. A single model is requested (not best_match) to keep the series homogeneous over 2018–2026.
  • Places fetched: the 20 most populous World Bank places plus the World Bank place nearest each Kaggle/HF city (≤ 25 km): 22 places in total. Fetched once by scripts/fetch_openmeteo_weather.py; raw JSON responses and a manifest (request/grid coordinates, retrieval time) are stored in data/raw/openmeteo_weather/. The dashboard never calls the API.

Placement instructions (manual download)

If the automated downloads fail, place files exactly here and run python scripts/prepare_data.py --extract:

data/raw/worldbank_pm25/PM25_Middle_East_North_Africa_Afghanistan_Pakistan.zip
data/raw/hf_pakistan_aq/pakistan_air_quality_final_clean.csv
data/raw/openmeteo_weather/   (run: python scripts/fetch_openmeteo_weather.py)

Only the World Bank file is required; the other two sources are optional and the app degrades gracefully without them.

Candidates investigated but not used

  • World Bank South Asia regional file — not needed (Pakistan is in the MENA file).
  • Zenodo / other Kaggle datasets — not searched exhaustively; no further dataset was added because none was verified for provenance, coverage and licence within this build.
data_dictionary:
Data dictionary

All processed tables live in data/processed/ (Parquet) and are rebuilt by python scripts/prepare_data.py. "Modelled" means model or reanalysis output — no field in this project is a monitor measurement.

wb_pm25_daily.parquet — World Bank daily PM2.5 (one row per place per day)

Field Type Unit Source Description / limitations
city_id category – derived wb:<geonameid>; stable key
geonameid int – WB GeoNames identifier of the place
city category – WB Place name after Unicode/whitespace/case normalisation
city_label category – derived Unique display label; shared names get (Province) or (lat°N, lon°E)
province category – derived Label inferred from adm1_code (see methodology); not an official boundary join
adm1_code category – WB adm1cd_c Source first-level admin code (PAK002…PAK007)
latitude, longitude float degrees WB Place coordinates as supplied (not corrected)
population int persons WB GeoNames population; vintage not documented
date datetime (naive) day WB Calendar day; day boundary/time zone undocumented by the source
pm25 float µg/m³ (assumed) WB Modelled daily mean PM2.5; never converted to AQI
source_id category – derived Always wb_pm25
value_type category – derived Always modelled
year, month int – derived Calendar fields from date
month_name category – derived Jan…Dec
season category – derived Winter (Dec–Feb), Spring (Mar–Apr), Pre-monsoon (May–Jun), Monsoon (Jul–Sep), Post-monsoon (Oct–Nov)
day_of_week category – derived Monday…Sunday
is_weekend bool – derived Saturday or Sunday (see caveat in methodology)
is_outlier bool – derived Robust z-score of log PM2.5 within city > 3.5; flagged, not removed

wb_cities.parquet — one row per World Bank place

Field Unit Description
city_id, geonameid, city, city_label, adm1_code, province, latitude, longitude, population – As above
n_days, first_date, last_date days / date Coverage of the place
name_ambiguous bool Another GeoNames ID shares the same normalised name (e.g. "Arif Wala"/"Arifwala")
coords_in_bbox bool Coordinates inside a generous Pakistan bounding box
series_group, series_group_size int Places whose full daily series is identical share a group (same model grid cell)
is_series_representative bool Most populous member of its series group; used for inferential tests
fixed_annual_run, fixed_annual_from, fixed_annual_to years Longest run of consecutive complete years with annual means within 0.5 %
break_date, break_shift, break_shift_rel, break_t date / µg/m³ / ratio / – Largest single level shift in deseasonalised monthly anomalies (screening scan)
mean_level µg/m³ Mean of complete monthly means
artifact_flag, artifact_reason bool / text Fixed annual mean ≥ 3 years and/or abrupt shift (t ≥ 10 and ≥ 30 % of level)

hf_hourly.parquet — Kaggle/HF hourly (one row per city per hour)

Field Unit Description / limitations
city_id – hf:<normalised name>
city, latitude, longitude – / degrees As supplied
timestamp naive datetime Source hour label, unchanged. Pollutant columns appear to be UTC and weather columns local time (diagnostic in Data Quality)
date, hour – Derived from timestamp
pm25, pm10, carbon_monoxide, nitrogen_dioxide, sulphur_dioxide, ozone, dust µg/m³ Modelled (probable CAMS); invalid cells set to NaN
temperature °C Hourly 2 m temperature (source undocumented)
humidity % Relative humidity
precipitation mm per hour
wind_speed km/h Units inferred from the Open-Meteo default; not documented by uploader
wind_direction °
pressure hPa
source_id, value_type – hf_aq, modelled
year, month, season, … – Calendar fields recomputed from timestamp

hf_daily.parquet — Kaggle/HF aggregated to days

Same variables as hourly. Rule: mean of hourly values (precipitation summed, wind direction circular mean) when ≥ 18 valid hours exist for that variable; otherwise NaN. n_hours records the hours present. Day boundaries follow the source's hour labels.

weather_daily.parquet — ERA5 daily weather per World Bank place

Field Unit Description
city_id, geonameid – World Bank place the weather was fetched for
date day Local (Asia/Karachi) day
temperature, temperature_max, temperature_min °C 2 m air temperature (daily mean/max/min)
humidity % Daily mean relative humidity at 2 m
dew_point °C Daily mean dew point at 2 m
wind_speed, wind_speed_max km/h 10 m wind speed (daily mean / max)
wind_direction ° Dominant 10 m wind direction
precipitation mm/day Daily total
pressure hPa Daily mean surface pressure
grid_latitude, grid_longitude, grid_elevation_m degrees / m ERA5 grid cell actually used
source_id, value_type – openmeteo_era5, modelled

wb_weather_daily.parquet

Inner join of wb_pm25_daily and weather_daily on (city_id, date); all fields of both, plus weather_grid_lat, weather_grid_lon, weather_source_id.

source_overlap_daily.parquet

Field Description
city_id, city Kaggle/HF city
match_city_id, match_city_label, distance_km Nearest World Bank place (≤ 25 km)
date Calendar date present in both sources
pm25_hf Kaggle/HF daily mean (µg/m³)
pm25_wb World Bank daily value (µg/m³)
n_hours Hours behind pm25_hf

The two PM2.5 values stay in separate columns: the table supports comparison only.

Pipeline outputs

  • exclusions_log.csv — every exclusion, nulling, flag and transformation: source, step, rule, column, rows affected, action, examples.
  • pipeline_manifest.json — run time, SHA-256 of raw inputs, row counts, rules, ADM1 anchor check.
